hints.title: Triad Product Rule
hints.text: The maximum product of three elements in any array is always either the product of the three largest values or the product of the two smallest values and the largest value.

hints.title: Single Replacement Simulation
hints.text: Substitute each position with the target replacement value and evaluate the maximal triplet product.

hints.title: Negative Multipliers
hints.text: Two large negative numbers multiplied by a large positive number yield a large positive product.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def maxProduct(self, nums: list[int], target: int) -> int:
        # Replace one element in nums with target to maximize product of three distinct elements
        n = len(nums)
        best = -float('inf')
        for i in range(n):
            # Form candidate array by replacing nums[i] with target
            cand = nums[:i] + [target] + nums[i+1:]
            cand.sort()
            prod1 = cand[-1] * cand[-2] * cand[-3]
            prod2 = cand[0] * cand[1] * cand[-1]
            best = max(best, prod1, prod2)
        return best
```

complexity.notes: Testing replacements across critical boundary elements.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Examining all O(N^4) combinations takes quartic time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Know the two-case formula for max product of 3 elements.
